subject: Agriculture
title: Minerals in Soil
description: A fast breakdown of Minerals in Soil for builders.

hook.text: About 45% of soil is mineral matter—tiny fragments of the rocks that once towered above.

buildup.text: Quartz, feldspar, and mica are common soil minerals. Each weathers differently and contributes different nutrients.

discovery.text: Clay minerals are special—their tiny, flat plates have enormous surface area that holds nutrients and water.

twist.text: Not all clays are equal. Montmorillonite swells when wet and cracks when dry. Kaolinite stays stable.

climax.text: The mineral mix determines what a soil can grow. Farmers can add nutrients, but can't change the minerals.

punchline.text: Every field is built on the bones of ancient mountains.

quiz.question: Why are clay minerals important in soil?
options: Their large surface area holds nutrients and water
